note: One case per Rust test of effect/program_eval.rs (missing_failure_is_an_error, no_options_object_is_an_error, empty_failure_event_is_an_error, control_with_failure_is_clean) plus the validate_emit_config checks program/eval runs on its emit option (unknown key, invalid identifier, undeclared event, non-string name) and the effect-sequencing walk. Expected findings are the code, path, message and suggestion the Rust validator reports, in the order validate_program_eval produces them (the emit keys first, the missing failure last). The effects are flattened by std-orb-effect-leaves: the rule asks with EFFECT_LEAVES_EXPAND and checks the leaves it answers. A branch that is null is no leaf, so a null else is neither a finding nor an unchecked node.

findings.message: `program/eval` carries no `emit.failure` event — the validator's errors come back through it and would be dropped
findings.suggestion: Add `{ emit: { success: "<EVENT>", failure: "<FAILURE_EVENT>" } }` as the last arg and handle the failure event in an arm.
